chapter.title: Things Around Us
chapter.tagline: Investigating buoyancy, float-or-sink experiments, density of salt water, and solar salt evaporation
chapter.overview: Why does a heavy iron ship float while a tiny steel sewing needle sinks immediately? Through kitchen and classroom science experiments, students explore buoyancy, dissolve spoons of salt in water to discover density changes, and learn how the famous Dead Sea lets humans float effortlessly.

sections.title: What Floats, What Sinks? Exploring Buoyancy
sections.subtitle: Understanding buoyant force, shape, and surface displacement

storyNarrative.dialogue: A crumpled ball of aluminum foil sinks, but when we flatten that exact same foil into a wide shallow boat, it floats carrying small pebbles! Shape matters!

concept.heading: Archimedes' Buoyancy Principle
concept.keyRule: An object floats if its shape displaces an amount of water equal to its own weight before becoming submerged.

questions.prompt: Why can a massive iron ship float on the ocean while a small iron nail sinks?
options: The ship is hollow and displaces a huge weight of water
Iron nails are heavier than ships
Ships are made of wood inside
questions.correctAnswer: The ship is hollow and displaces a huge weight of water
questions.hint: The hollow shape gives the ship a huge buoyant displacement.

sections.title: The Salt Water Mystery: Floating an Egg
sections.subtitle: How dissolving solute alters liquid density and buoyant lift

storyNarrative.dialogue: Our fresh egg sank straight to the bottom of the plain water glass. But when Ayesha stirred 4 big spoons of salt into the water, the egg bobbed right up to the top!

concept.heading: Liquid Density Enhancement
concept.keyRule: Dissolving salt adds mass without significantly increasing volume, increasing the water's density and its upward buoyant force.

sections.title: The Dead Sea & Solar Salt Pans
sections.subtitle: Natural hyper-saline lakes and coastal salt harvesting

storyNarrative.dialogue: In the Dead Sea, water has about 300 grams of salt in every single litre! A person can lie on their back reading a book without swimming and never sink!

concept.heading: Hyper-Salinity & Solar Crystallization
concept.keyRule: In coastal salt pans, seawater is trapped in shallow basins; intense sunlight evaporates water, leaving behind crystallized edible salt.
